extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of classical geometry; readers of Euclid's Elements
extracted.subtask_description: Collection of Euclid Book V propositions about ratios and magnitudes: precise theorems relating equimultiples, equality/inequality, inversion/composition of ratios, and how proportion relationships propagate under various constructions. Useful for formal reasoning about proportionality of magnitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. V. THEOR.
rubrics_metrics.description: IF one magnitude be the same multiple of another, which a magnitude taken from the first is of a magnitude taken from the other; the remainder shall be the same multiple of the remainder, that the whole is of the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: Let AB be the same multiple of CD that AE (taken from AB) is of CF (taken from CD); then remainder EB is the same multiple of FD that AB is of CD. Proof sketch: construct corresponding multiples, use equality of constructed multiples and subtract common part (AE) to deduce equality of remainders and then the multiplicity relation for the remainders. (Full proof given in text.)

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. VI. THEOR.
rubrics_metrics.description: IF two magnitudes be equimultiples of two others, and if equimultiples of these be taken from the first two, the remainders are either equal to these others, or equimultiples of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: If AB, CD are equimultiples of E, F, and AG, CH (taken from AB, CD) are equimultiples of the same E, F, then remainders GB, HD are either equal to E, F or equimultiples of them. Proof gives separate cases: when remainders equal the base magnitudes, and when they are multiples; constructs matching multiples and uses prior propositions and subtraction of common parts to deduce conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. A. THEOR.
rubrics_metrics.description: IF the first of four magnitudes has to the second the same ratio which the third has to the fourth ; then, if the first be greater than the second, the third is also greater than the fourth; and, if equal, equal; if less, less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: If A:B = C:D and A > B then C > D (and similar for equality/less). Proof idea: take any equimultiples (e.g. doubles), use definition of comparison of equimultiples to propagate inequality from one pair to the other; argument handles equal/less similarly.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. B. THEOR.
rubrics_metrics.description: IF four magnitudes are proportionals, they are proportionals also when taken inversely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: If A:B = C:D then B:A = D:C. Proof: take equimultiples of B,D and of A,C and compare; using definition of proportion via equimultiples, show inequalities/equalities of those equimultiples correspond, hence the inverse proportion holds.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. C. THEOR.
rubrics_metrics.description: IF the first be the same multiple of the second, or the same part of it, that the third is of the fourth ; the first is to the second as the third is to the fourth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement covers two cases: (1) when A is the same multiple of B that C is of D, then A:B = C:D; (2) when A is the same part of B that C is of D, then likewise. Proof: take arbitrary equimultiples of A,C and of B,D and use known multiplicity relations to show comparisons of equimultiples match; handles 'part' case by inversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. D. THEOR.
rubrics_metrics.description: IF the first be to the second as the third to the fourth, and if the first be a multiple, or part, of the second; the third is the same multiple, or the same part, of the fourth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: From A:B = C:D and the additional fact that A is a multiple (or part) of B, deduce C is the same multiple (or same part) of D. Proof: construct appropriate equimultiples and use equality and inversion/composition arguments to transfer multiplicity/part relation.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. Vn. THEOR.
rubrics_metrics.description: EQUAL magnitudes have the same ratio to the same magnitude ; and the same has the same ratio to equal magnitudes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: If A = B then A:C = B:C and C:A = C:B for any C. Proof: choose equimultiples of A,B and any multiple of C; equality of A and B makes their equimultiples equal, so comparisons to multiples of C are identical; similarly for C to A/B.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. Vin. THEOR.
rubrics_metrics.description: OF unequal magnitudes, the greater has a greater ratio to the same than the less has ; and the same magnitude has a greater ratio to the less, than it has to the greater.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: If AB > BC then AB:C > BC:C; and for fixed D, D:BC > D:AB. Proof: multiply the lesser magnitude until it exceeds the third, take corresponding multiples, use least multiple of D greater than FG to create comparison, then deduce which ratio is greater using equimultiple comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. IX. THEOR.
rubrics_metrics.description: MAGNITUDES which have the same ratio to the same magnitude are equal to one another; and those to which the same magnitude has the same ratio are equal to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: If A:C = B:C then A = B; and if C:A = C:B then A = B. Proof by contradiction using equimultiples: if A > B (or vice versa) produce equimultiples that violate the assumed equality of ratios, yielding impossibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. X. THEOR.
rubrics_metrics.description: THAT magnitude which has a greater ratio than another has unto the same magnitude is the greater of the two : and that magnitude, to which the same has a greater ratio than it has unto another magnitude, is the lesser of the two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: If A:C > B:C then A > B; and if C:B > C:A then B < A. Proof: use existence of equimultiples and a multiple of C with comparative inequalities to deduce ordering of A and B from ordering of their equimultiples.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XI. THEOR. (labeled 'XL' in text)
rubrics_metrics.description: RATIOS that are the same to the same ratio are the same to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: If A:B = C:D and C:D = E:F then A:B = E:F. Proof: take equimultiples of A,C,E and of B,D,F and propagate the 'greater/equal/less' relationships transitively using the two given proportionalities to conclude comparisons between arbitrary equimultiples of A,E and B,F match, hence the ratios are the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XII. THEOR.
rubrics_metrics.description: IF any number of magnitudes be proportionals, as one of the antecedents is to its consequent, so shall all the antecedents taken together be to all the consequents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: For magnitudes A:B :: C:D :: E:F, the combined antecedents A,C,E are to combined consequents B,D,F as A is to B. Proof: take arbitrary equimultiples of each and of each consequent, show componentwise comparisons produce the same 'greater/equal/less' result for sums (totals) and thus the combined ratio follows.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XIII. THEOR.
rubrics_metrics.description: IF the first has to the second the same ratio which the third has to the fourth, but the third to the fourth a greater ratio than the fifth has to the sixth; the first shall also have to the second a greater ratio than the fifth has to the sixth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: From A:B = C:D and C:D > E:F deduce A:B > E:F. Proof: choose equimultiples illustrating C:D > E:F and map those multiples to corresponding multiples of A,B to transfer the inequality; corollary gives similar variant when ordering of which pairs share equality/inequality is permuted.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XIV. THEOR.
rubrics_metrics.description: IF the first has to the second the same ratio which the third has to the fourth; then, if the first be greater than the third, the second shall be greater than the fourth; and if equal, equal; and if less, less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: From A:B = C:D and A > C deduce B > D (and analogously for equality/less). Proof: use that A:C ordering implies A:B vs C:B ordering by earlier propositions and deduce converse ordering of the corresponding consequents.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XV. THEOR.
rubrics_metrics.description: MAGNITUDES have the same ratio to one another which their equimultiples have.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: If AB is the same multiple of C that DE is of F, then C:F = AB:DE. Proof: decompose AB into equal parts each equal to C and DE into equal parts each equal to F; compare corresponding equal parts and then apply the result that sums of equal antecedents to consequents have the same ratio.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XVI. THEOR.
rubrics_metrics.description: IF four magnitudes of the same kind be proportionals, they shall also be proportionals when taken alternately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: If A:B = C:D then A:C = B:D. Proof: take arbitrary equimultiples of A,B and of C,D and use Proposition XV (equimultiples preserve ratios) and Proposition XIV (inequalities propagate) to transform and compare equimultiples pairwise, yielding the alternate proportion.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XVII. THEOR.
rubrics_metrics.description: IF magnitudes, taken jointly, be proportionals, they shall also be proportionals when taken separately; that is, if two magnitudes together have to one of them the same ratio which two others have to one of these, the remaining one of the first two shall have to the other the same ratio which the remaining one of the last two has to the other of these.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement (example form): If AB:BE = CD:DF then AE:EB = CF:FD. Proof: take equimultiples of the separate pieces and of the others; construct equimultiples and use composition/subtraction to obtain equimultiples of the joint magnitudes, then apply comparison logic to deduce the separate proportion.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XVIII. THEOR.
rubrics_metrics.description: IF magnitudes, taken separately, be proportionals, they shall also be proportionals when taken jointly, that is, if the first be to the second, as the third to the fourth, the first and second together shall be to the second, as the third and fourth together to the fourth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement (example form): If AE:EB = CF:FD then AB:BE = CD:DF. Proof: consider arbitrary equimultiples of pieces and of wholes, compare cases KO ≤ KH or KO > KH (notations from proof) to show the sums (joint magnitudes) preserve the proportional relation; detailed case analysis in text.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XIX. THEOR.
rubrics_metrics.description: IF a whole magnitude be to a whole, as a magnitude taken from the first is to a magnitude taken from the other ; the remainder shall be to the remainder, as the whole to the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: If AB:CD = AE:CF (AE taken from AB, CF from CD) then EB:FD = AB:CD. Proof: use alternation and the fact that jointly-taken proportions imply separately-taken ones (previous propositions) to rearrange and deduce the ratio of remainders equals ratio of wholes.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. E. THEOR.
rubrics_metrics.description: IF four magnitudes be proportionals, they are also proportionals by conversion, that is, the first is to its excess above the second, as the third to its excess above the fourth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: If AB:BE = CD:DF then BA:AE = DC:CF. Proof: use division and inversion to re-express the given proportion and then composition to obtain the converted proportion; short derivation provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XX. THEOR.
rubrics_metrics.description: IF there be three magnitudes, and other three, which, taken two and two, have the same ratio ; if the first be greater than the third, the fourth shall be greater than the sixth ; and if equal, equal ; and if less, less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: For A,B,C and D,E,F with A:B = D:E and B:C = E:F, ordering (>,=,<) of A vs C implies same ordering of D vs F. Proof: combine earlier results about greater ratios implying greater magnitudes and use inversion/composition of proportionalities; handles equal and less cases similarly.
